title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Unsloth GGUF on llama.cpp, DGX Spark
slug_note: The plain Q4_K_M of the 35B-A3B MoE on the Spark: 66 tok/s, 23 GiB — the baseline lane against the MTP and Ollama rows.

variation.revision_note: HF snapshot resolved and served on the Spark during the 2026-10-27 test

requirements.notes: Measured on a DGX Spark (2026-10-27): 23.2 GiB dropped from MemAvailable with the recipe as written (--ctx-size 8192).

measurements.method: SR-101 bug-fix test: 6 small Python programs with a planted bug; the model returns fixed code, graded by hidden tests in docker (python:3.12-slim, no network, 512 MB); max_tokens 6000, temperature 0.3, one attempt per task; llama-server -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf -ngl 99 -fa on -c 65536 -np 4 --jinja --seed 42, llama.cpp build 12035 (commit 4e910a86e)
measurements.note: Single run. The one failure (task B3) ran out of its 6,000-token budget while thinking and returned no code; it was not a wrong fix.

caveats: Works as written on a DGX Spark (2026-10-27): `llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q4_K_M --ctx-size 8192 -ngl 99` — llama.cpp build 11866 (commit 3f03b1772); server ready 30 s after start with the OS file cache dropped; the functional check passed; MemAvailable dropped 23.2 GiB (weights + KV at --ctx-size 8192).

Same checkpoint family as the Ollama qwen3.6:35b-a3b lane measured on the Spark on 2026-10-26 (90.5 tok/s short prompt at Ollama's 262,144-token default context): llama.cpp here ran at 8,192 context for comparability with the rest of the queue, so the two rows are not a fair engine A/B (different context, different resident KV).

Room load test (2026-11-03, single run, n=1 per level): per-user decode 66.9 / 19.0 / 12.0 / 7.3 tok/s at 1 / 10 / 20 / 40 users at once; the box total was 66.6 / 189.2 / 238.7 / 289.8 tok/s. Against a 10 tok/s reading-speed bar, 20 users stay above it (12.0 each) and 40 fall below (7.3). Measured with -c 327680 -np 40 (40 parallel slots), not the command above, which serves the default number of slots.

Bug-fix test (2026-11-04, single run): 5 of 6 small Python bug fixes passed hidden tests, served with -c 65536 -np 4 -fa on. The miss ran out of tokens while thinking, so a larger max_tokens may change it.
